```{r setup, include=FALSE}

gc()

load.lib <- c("tidyverse", "data.table", "sf", "here")

install.lib <- load.lib[!load.lib %in% installed.packages()]
```

# Verify data

The data stored and originally accessed on ERDDAP has moved to www.fisheries.noaa.gov/import/item/20693 and has changed since the start of the study. To verify that the original files are correct check the CPS_Trawl_Life_History_Haul_Catch_Data.csv and the CPS_Trawl_Life_History_Specimen_Data.csv and adjust accordingly.

# From the CPS_Trawl_LifeHistory_Haulcatch Table:

1) subsample_weight: Description - Summed weight of all *xth* individuals listed in the subsample_count column. Units - kg. Note - Five random full baskets from the entire catch (all species) are take as a subsample. Subsample weight is almost never extrapolated (except when there are > 5 baskets). Following sorting of species, if there are > 75 individuals in a basket for example, remaining_weight becomes the unsampled weight for that species. To get total weight of species in a given haul, sum subsample_weight and remaining_weight.
       
# From the CPS_Trawl_LifeHistory_Specimen Table:

1) weight: Description - The weight of an individual of species *e* in the subsample *i* randomly selected
Units - g. Note - There may be a mix of other species included in the data and it is important to compare the subsample_weight to the sum of individual measures weights for species *e*.
       
2) Length: Description - The length of an individual of species *e* in the subsample *i* randomly selected. Units - mm. Note - Note that depending on the species, this can be standard length (SL) or fork length (FL).
       
# Load and explore haul catch data

```{r, read.haul.data}

# Load catch weight
LifeHistoryHaulCatch <- 
  fread(
    here(dir, "Data", survey.path,
         "CPS_Trawl_LifeHistory_Haulcatch.new.server.version.csv"), 
        sep = ",") 

colnames(LifeHistoryHaulCatch)
#  [1] "cruise"                  "ship"                   
#  [3] "haul"                    "collection"             
#  [5] "startLatitude"           "startLongitude"         
#  [7] "stopLatitude"            "stopLongitude"          
#  [9] "equilibriumTime"         "haulBackTime"           
# [11] "surfaceTemp"             "surfaceTempMethod"      
# [13] "shipSpeedThrougtheWater" "itisTSN"                
# [15] "scientificName"          "subSampleCount"         
# [17] "subSampleWeightkg"       "remainingWeightkg"      
# [19] "presenceOnly"           

# Remove unnescessary columns
LifeHistoryHaulCatch <- LifeHistoryHaulCatch[,-c(11:13,19)]

# Rename to match old data version for consistency 
names(LifeHistoryHaulCatch) <- 
  c("cruise", "ship", "haul", "collection", 
    "start_latitude", "start_longitude", 
    "stop_latitude", "stop_longitude",
    "equilibrium_time", "haulback_time",
    "itis_tsn", "scientific_name",
    "subsample_count", "subsample_weight",
    "remaining_weight"
    )

LifeHistoryHaulCatch <- LifeHistoryHaulCatch %>%
  mutate(keys.temp = paste(cruise, ship, haul, collection,
                           itis_tsn, equilibrium_time, 
                           sep = ""),
         keys = paste(cruise, ship, haul, collection,
                      itis_tsn, equilibrium_time, 
                      start_latitude, start_longitude, 
                      stop_latitude, stop_longitude, 
                      sep = "_")
         )

# Not all hauls have a remaining_weight (force these values to 0)
LifeHistoryHaulCatch$remaining_weight[is.na(LifeHistoryHaulCatch$remaining_weight)] <- 0

# Explore data
length(unique(LifeHistoryHaulCatch$cruise))
# [1] 36 (35 in old version)
length(unique(LifeHistoryHaulCatch$collection))
# [1] 2780 (2676 in old version)
length(unique(LifeHistoryHaulCatch$ship))
# [1] 8 (8 in old version)
length(unique(LifeHistoryHaulCatch$itis_tsn))
# [1] 273 (266 in old version)

# Bind coordinates
LifeHistoryHaulCatch <- LifeHistoryHaulCatch %>% 
  mutate(beginTransect = 
           paste(start_longitude, ",", start_latitude, sep = ""), 
         endTransect = 
           paste(stop_longitude, ",", stop_latitude, sep = "")) %>%
  mutate(transect.coords = 
           paste(beginTransect, ",", endTransect, sep = ""))

length(unique(LifeHistoryHaulCatch$transect.coords))
# [1] 2780 (2676 in old version)

colnames(LifeHistoryHaulCatch)
#  [1] "cruise"           "ship"             "haul"            
#  [4] "collection"       "start_latitude"   "start_longitude" 
#  [7] "stop_latitude"    "stop_longitude"   "equilibrium_time"
# [10] "haulback_time"    "itis_tsn"         "scientific_name" 
# [13] "subsample_count"  "subsample_weight" "remaining_weight"
# [16] "beginTransect"    "endTransect"      "transect.coords"

unique(is.na(LifeHistoryHaulCatch))

# Add time zone to column name
LifeHistoryHaulCatch <- LifeHistoryHaulCatch %>%
  mutate(
    haulback_time.utc = haulback_time,
    equilibrium_time.utc = equilibrium_time) %>%
  select(-c(haulback_time, equilibrium_time))

summary(LifeHistoryHaulCatch)

sum.tab <- LifeHistoryHaulCatch %>% 
  group_by(equilibrium_time.utc) %>%
  mutate(collect.check = n_distinct(collection)) %>%
  ungroup()

sum.tab.check <- sum.tab %>% 
  filter(collect.check > 1)

dim(sum.tab.check)
# [1] 31 21

```

# Merge specimen and haul data

```{r, catch.per.haul}

# Find like column ids
colnames(LifeHistorySpecimen) %in% colnames(LifeHistoryHaulCatch)
#  [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
# [11] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE

# View names of column ids
joinKeys <- LifeHistorySpecimen %>% select(c(1:4,8:9)) %>%
  names()
joinKeys
# [1] "cruise"          "ship"            "haul"           
# [4] "collection"      "itis_tsn"        "scientific_name"

# Join data sets by column ids and calculate haul expansion factor
CatchWeightLengthPerHaul <- inner_join(LifeHistoryHaulCatch,
                                       LifeHistorySpecimen, 
                                       by = joinKeys) %>% 
  distinct()

summary(CatchWeightLengthPerHaul)

# View the random sample notations
unique(CatchWeightLengthPerHaul$is_random_sample)
# [1] "Y" "N" NA

# How many unique collections
length(unique(CatchWeightLengthPerHaul$collection))
# [1] 1998

# Check if keys.temp is identical between files
identical(CatchWeightLengthPerHaul$keys.temp.x, 
          CatchWeightLengthPerHaul$keys.temp.y) 
# [1] TRUE
# This confirms that time is equivalent to equilibrium time

# Remove extra column
CatchWeightLengthPerHaul <-
  CatchWeightLengthPerHaul[,-c("time", "keys.temp.x", "keys.temp.y")]

```

# Apply quality check of remaining sample data

## Create indices

If the total sampled weight is equal to the subsample_weight, they the quality index is 0. Otherwise, it means there is a discrepancy.

```{r, all.other.specimen.entries}

#-------------------------------
# For Sardine
#-------------------------------
Haul.weights.sar <- CatchWeightLengthPerHaul %>%
  # Isolate only sardine
  filter(scientific_name == "Sardinops sagax" &
           # Filter out known issues
           !is.na(subsample_weight)) 

#-------------------------------
# Make sure random samples are 
# not already present
#-------------------------------
match.keys <- no.sardine.subsample.weights.fin %>%
  filter(keys %in% Haul.weights.sar$keys)
dim(match.keys)
# [1]  0 25

#-------------------------------
# Join with adjusted 
# sardine.subsample.weights.fin
#-------------------------------
Haul.weights.sar <- rbind(Haul.weights.sar, 
                          no.sardine.subsample.weights.fin
                          ) %>%
  # Make sure they are unique
  distinct()

#-------------------------------
# Create quality.index
#-------------------------------
Haul.weights.sar <- Haul.weights.sar %>%
  # Group by transect
  group_by(keys) %>% 
  # Sum the sampled and unsampled species weight to get total 
  # species weight
  mutate(Species_weight = subsample_weight+remaining_weight,
         # Convert g to kg for individual samples
         weight = 
           case_when(!is.na(weight) ~ weight/1000,
                     is.na(weight) ~ NA
                     )
         ) %>% 
  # See if the summed specimen weight is less than or greater 
  # than total weight of the random sample
  mutate(quality.indic = round(sum(weight)-subsample_weight,3)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(FID = seq(1,nrow(.),1))

#-------------------------------
# How many hauls with 
# corresponding specimen 
# data?
#-------------------------------
dim(Haul.weights.sar)
# [1] 18500    28

```

## Check quality indices

First double check the data where the quality indices are 0. Do they make sense? Are there missing values, etc.?

### Check the entries with quality indices of 0

```{r, double.check.sardine.quality.indices}

#-------------------------------
# How many hauls with
# corresponding specimen
# data and quality indices
# are equal to zero?
#-------------------------------
Haul.weights.sar.clean <- 
  Haul.weights.sar %>%
  filter(quality.indic == 0) 

dim(Haul.weights.sar.clean)
# [1] 13184    28

#-------------------------------
# How many hauls with
# corresponding specimen
# data and quality indices
# are equal to zero and
# where number of entries 
# equal the sample count
#-------------------------------
Haul.weights.sar %>%
  filter(quality.indic == 0) %>%
  group_by(keys) %>%
  filter(max(specimen_number) ==
           subsample_count) %>%
  dim()
# [1] 12745  28

#-------------------------------
# Investigate hauls with
# corresponding specimen
# data and quality indices
# equal to zero, but where number 
# of entries is not equal the 
# sample count
#-------------------------------
test.quality.good.but.bad.spec <-
  Haul.weights.sar %>%
  filter(quality.indic == 0) %>%
  group_by(keys) %>%
  filter(max(specimen_number) !=
           subsample_count) %>%
  ungroup()
# View(test.quality.good.but.bad.spec)

# It seems there have been some 
# samples removed, but they have 
# already been accounted for in 
# the weight proportioning

#----------------------------------
# Investigate na values
#----------------------------------
unique(is.na(Haul.weights.sar.clean))
# looks like we are no longer missing
# individual specimen weights, but 
# we have some cases we do not know
# length

#----------------------------------
# How do the weights look
#----------------------------------
Haul.weights.sar.clean2 <- 
  Haul.weights.sar.clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(standard_length))

range(Haul.weights.sar.clean2$weight)
# [1] 0.0005 0.3395
# View(Haul.weights.sar.clean2)

# These really small weights are for
# sardines less than 4 cm in length
# and describes poorly conditioned
# post-larval phase individuals

```

### Check the entries with quality indices not equal to 0

This will isolate cases where subsample weight total specimen weight don't match.

#### For historic paper write up, filter out the viable cruises

Note: keep all the data because a follow up study will be done and we will need all years for that!

```{r, historic.paper}

colnames(CatchWeightLengthPerHaul)
unique(CatchWeightLengthPerHaul$scientific_name)

# Find the number of hauls with corresponding specimens
test.total.hauls <- CatchWeightLengthPerHaul %>%
  filter(cruise > 200804 & cruise < 202103) %>%
  filter(!cruise %in% c(200904, 201004, 201104, 201204, 201304, 201404, 
                        201504, 201604, 201704))
length(unique(test.total.hauls$keys))
# [1] 2236

# Find the number of hauls without corresponding specimens
test.hauls.no.specimens <- no.specimen.dat %>%
  filter(cruise > 200804 & cruise < 202103) %>%
  filter(!cruise %in% c(200904, 201004, 201104, 201204, 201304, 201404, 
                        201504, 201604, 201704))
length(unique(test.hauls.no.specimens$keys))
# [1] 4


test <- Haul.weights.sar %>%
  filter(cruise > 200804 & cruise < 202103) %>%
  filter(!cruise %in% c(200904, 201004, 201104, 201204, 201304, 201404, 
                        201504, 201604, 201704))
length(unique(test$keys))
# [1] 300

test2 <- test %>%
  filter(quality.indic != 0 | is.na(quality.indic))
length(unique(test2$keys))
# [1] 10
length(unique(test2$keys))/length(unique(test$keys))*100
# [1] 3.333333

test3 <- test %>% filter(is.na(standard_length))
length(unique(test3$keys))
# [1] 2 

test4 <- test2 %>% 
  filter(max(specimen_number) > subsample_count)
length(unique(test4$keys))
# [1] 10

test5 <- test4 %>%
  filter(specimen_number <= subsample_count) %>% 
  mutate(quality.indic2 = 
           round(sum(weight)-subsample_weight, 3)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct() %>% 
  filter(quality.indic2 != 0)
length(unique(test5$keys))
```

#### Check if there are excess specimens

```{r, extra.specimens}

#--------------------------------------------
# Find how many entries exceed the sample 
# count
#--------------------------------------------
extra.specimens <- quality.chcks %>%
  group_by(keys) %>%
  # Find entries where the max specimen number is more 
  # than the number of sampled individuals
  filter(max(specimen_number) > subsample_count)

dim(extra.specimens)
# [1] 4794  28
# View(extra.specimens)

length(unique(extra.specimens$keys))

fwrite(extra.specimens, here(dir, "Data", survey.path,
                  "ATM.Survey.extra.sample.observation.csv"),
       sep = ",")

# For the historic paper
historic.extra.specimens <- extra.specimens %>%
  filter(cruise > 200804 & cruise < 202103) %>%
  filter(!cruise %in% c(200904, 201004, 201104, 201204, 201304, 201404, 
                        201504, 201604, 201704))
length(unique(historic.extra.specimens$keys))
# [1] 7

#--------------------------------------------
# Recalculate the quality indices after 
# filtering out extra samples and see if that helps
#--------------------------------------------
extra.specimens.resolved <- 
  extra.specimens %>%
  group_by(keys) %>%
  # Remove individuals exceeding the total sample count
  filter(specimen_number <= subsample_count) %>% 
  mutate(quality.indic2 = 
           round(sum(weight)-subsample_weight, 3)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct()

#--------------------------------------------
# Save entries where this fixed the problem
#--------------------------------------------
extra.specimens.resolved.ok <- 
  extra.specimens.resolved %>% 
  filter(quality.indic2 == 0)

dim(extra.specimens.resolved.ok)
# [1] 3481   29

#--------------------------------------------
# Isolate cases, where this did not solve the 
# problem
#--------------------------------------------
extra.specimens.cont. <- 
  extra.specimens.resolved %>% 
  filter(quality.indic2 != 0)

dim(extra.specimens.cont.)
# [1] 432  29

length(unique(extra.specimens.cont.$keys))
# [1] 10

# What is the range we are now working with
range(extra.specimens.cont.$quality.indic2)
# [1] -6.937  2.359

# What keys are represented?
unique(extra.specimens.cont.$keys)
#  [1] "200307_FR_32_2034_161729_2003-07-20 06:50:00_44.1466_-124.4486_44.1106_-124.4436"
#  [2] "200403_FR_55_2105_161729_2004-03-17 12:37:00_46.101_-124.3756_46.1331_-124.3803" 
#  [3] "200404_FR_21_2131_161729_2004-04-27 11:53:00_35.8958_-123.9646_35.8245_-123.9296"
#  [4] "200407_FR_29_2164_161729_2004-07-16 09:18:00_44.0006_-124.5733_43.9993_-124.6311"
#  [5] "200407_FR_53_2188_161729_2004-07-23 07:35:00_42.5798_-125.345_42.5333_-125.3365" 
#  [6] "200503_FR_4_2197_161729_2005-03-04 07:00:00_47.9985_-126.5163_48.006_-126.5593"  
#  [7] "200503_FR_36_2229_161729_2005-03-15 06:00:00_43.0006_-124.8486_42.9715_-124.8605"
#  [8] "200504_JD_10_2252_161729_2005-04-06 05:21:00_34.5295_-121.0698_34.5015_-121.049" 
#  [9] "200706_MF_4_2289_161729_2007-06-07 09:43:00_46.0288_-125.3115_46.0525_-125.3373" 
# [10] "200407_FR_26_2161_161729_2004-07-15 12:32:00_45.0096_-124.34_44.9621_-124.3388"

# Check that there are no keys shared between the two sets
keys.check.extra.specimens.cont. <-
  extra.specimens.cont. %>%
  filter(keys %in% extra.specimens.resolved.ok$keys)

length(unique(keys.check.extra.specimens.cont.$keys))
# [1] 0

# For the historic paper
historic.extra.specimens.cont. <- extra.specimens.cont. %>%
  filter(cruise > 200804 & cruise < 202103) %>%
  filter(!cruise %in% c(200904, 201004, 201104, 201204, 201304, 201404, 
                        201504, 201604, 201704))
length(unique(historic.extra.specimens.cont.$keys))
# [1] 0

#--------------------------------------------
# So there are no shared keys between the two
# sets of data.
#--------------------------------------------
# Check if there is both random and 
# non-random samples
both.samp.types.extra.specimens.cont. <-
  extra.specimens.cont. %>%
  group_by(keys) %>%
  mutate(SampTypesOK =
          n_distinct(is_random_sample) == 2) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(SampTypesOK == TRUE)

dim(both.samp.types.extra.specimens.cont.) 
# [1] 0  30
# So there are no case where both random and 
# non-random samples exist

#--------------------------------------------
# There is an obvious weight error in 
# keys "200407_FR_26_2161_161729_2004-07-15 12:32:00_45.0096_-124.34_44.9621_-124.3388".
# In this haul, weight was already in kg so change
# it back.
extra.specimens.cont.fix <- extra.specimens.cont. %>%
  filter(keys == "200407_FR_26_2161_161729_2004-07-15 12:32:00_45.0096_-124.34_44.9621_-124.3388") %>%
  mutate(weight = weight*1000) %>%
  # Recalculate quality indices
  mutate(quality.indic2 = round(sum(weight)-subsample_weight,3))

head(extra.specimens.cont.fix)

#--------------------------------------------
# Add this haul back to the data
#--------------------------------------------
extra.specimens.cont.pt2 <- 
  extra.specimens.cont. %>%
  filter(keys != "200407_FR_26_2161_161729_2004-07-15 12:32:00_45.0096_-124.34_44.9621_-124.3388") %>%
  rbind(.,extra.specimens.cont.fix)

range(extra.specimens.cont.pt2$quality.indic2)
# [1] -2.807  2.359

#--------------------------------------------
# For remaining entries, redistribute weight
#--------------------------------------------
extra.specimens.cont.resolved <- 
  extra.specimens.cont.pt2 %>% 
  group_by(keys) %>%
  mutate(prop.len.wgt = weight/sum(weight)) %>%
  mutate(new.wgt = subsample_weight*prop.len.wgt) %>%
  mutate(quality.indic3 = round(sum(new.wgt)-subsample_weight,3))

unique(extra.specimens.cont.resolved$quality.indic3)
# [1] 0
dim(extra.specimens.cont.resolved)
# [1] 432   32

```

# Clean and the remaining data

```{r, other.species.prep}

# For Other species
Haul.weights.oth <- CatchWeightLengthPerHaul %>%
  # All but sardine
  filter(scientific_name != "Sardinops sagax") %>% 
  # Group by transect
  group_by(keys) %>% 
  mutate(#Simplify the names for uninterested species
         scientific_name = "Other",
         is_random_sample = NA,
         # Set to zero because we only want this as a place holder
         Species_weight = 0, 
         # Set to zero because we only want this as a place holder
         weight = 0,
         # Set to zero because we only want this as a place holder
         subsample_weight = 0,
         # Set to zero because we only want this as a place holder
         specimen_number = NA,
         # Set to zero because we only want this as a place holder
         subsample_count = 0,
         standard_length = NA) %>% 
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct()

dim(Haul.weights.oth)
```

# Join data sets

```{r, joindata}

#-------------------------------------
# For Sardines where things worked
## Note the observations with missing 
## lengths are removed.
#-------------------------------------
Haul.weights.sar.clean2.fin <- 
  Haul.weights.sar.clean2 %>% 
  filter(quality.indic == 0) %>%
  select(-c(FID, quality.indic))

#-------------------------------------
# For instances where removing the 
# surplus of sardine samples not 
# accounted for in the subsample weight
#-------------------------------------
extra.specimens.resolved.ok.fin <- 
  extra.specimens.resolved.ok %>%
  select(-c(FID, quality.indic2, 
            quality.indic))

#-------------------------------------
# For instances where removing the 
# surplus of sardine samples not 
# accounted for in the subsample weight
# and for correcting unit weights before
# redistribution weights within the haul
#-------------------------------------
extra.specimens.cont.resolved.fin <- 
  extra.specimens.cont.resolved %>%
  select(-c(FID, quality.indic2, 
            quality.indic3, 
            new.wgt, prop.len.wgt, 
            quality.indic))

#-------------------------------------
# For instances where there was no issue
# issue in number of samples, but there
# was a slight difference between the 
# total subsample weight and sum of 
# individual specimen weights
#-------------------------------------
Haul.weights.sar.remaining.2.test.resolved.fin <-
  Haul.weights.sar.remaining.2.test.resolved %>%
  select(-c(FID, quality.indic4, prop.len.wgt, 
            quality.indic))


US.specimen.dat.clean <-
  rbind(
    Haul.weights.sar.clean2.fin,
    extra.specimens.resolved.ok.fin,
    extra.specimens.cont.resolved.fin,
    Haul.weights.sar.remaining.2.test.resolved.fin,
    Haul.weights.oth)

dim(US.specimen.dat.clean)
# [1] 21105  26

fwrite(US.specimen.dat.clean, 
       here(dir, "Data", survey.path,
            "2003.2024.ATM.Survey.with.specimen.data.csv"), 
       sep = ",")

```
